review.words: For all $n\ge 2k$ the least prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$ is $\le\max(n/k,k)$, with only finitely many exceptions.

statement.text:
import Mathlib
import Nodes.«erdos-1094--h2--h2--h5--h2--h1».Context

open scoped Nat

/-! Hole `h_split` of a merged partial proof, as a node (D-12 #5, D-29).
Statement generated by the gate from the assembly; immutable (D-3). -/

theorem erdos_1094__h2__h2__h5__h2__h1 : ∀ (c : ℝ),
  (0 : ℝ) < c →
    ∀ (n k : ℕ),
      (0 : ℕ) < k →
        k ≤ n →
          (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → k < p → p ≤ n / k → ∀ (m : ℕ), n - k < m → m ≤ n → ¬p ∣ m) →
            ∀ (m : ℕ),
              n - k < m →
                m ≤ n →
                  ∏ p ∈ Finset.Icc (1 : ℕ) k with Nat.Prime p, p ^ (m.factorization : ℕ → ℕ) p = m ∨
                    ∏ p ∈ Finset.Icc (1 : ℕ) k with Nat.Prime p, p ^ (m.factorization : ℕ → ℕ) p < k := by
  sorry

open scoped Nat

theorem witness : ∃ (c : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (k : ℕ) (m : ℕ), (0 : ℝ) < c ∧ (0 : ℕ) < k ∧ k ≤ n ∧
    (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → k < p → p ≤ n / k → ∀ (m : ℕ), n - k < m → m ≤ n → ¬p ∣ m) ∧ n - k < m ∧ m ≤ n :=
  ⟨1, 1, 1, 1, one_pos, one_pos, le_rfl, fun _p _ h1 h2 _ _ _ _ => absurd (lt_of_lt_of_le h1 h2) (lt_irrefl _), by norm_num, le_rfl⟩
